block_summary:
**Triage Summary:**

Six duplicate findings all report CVE-2022-22965 (Spring Framework RCE) across Spring Boot and Spring Framework components at versions 2.2.2 and 5.2.2—this is a single critical vulnerability with EPSS 0.997 and active exploitation (KEV). A seventh finding flags CVE-2020-15999 (libfreetype6 RCE) with lower but still significant risk (EPSS 0.506). Both vulnerabilities have available fixes and are actively exploited in the wild.

**Recommended Action:** Upgrade Spring Boot to ≥2.6.x and Spring Framework to ≥5.3.x immediately to patch CVE-2022-22965, and update libfreetype6 to the latest patched version. These are not acceptable risks for production; treat as blocking unless there is documented compensating control (e.g., WAF rules blocking ClassPathXmlApplicationContext exploitation patterns).
review_summary:
**Triage Summary:**

This build contains multiple critical vulnerabilities across foundational system libraries (OpenSSL/libssl1.1, SQLite/libdb5.3, libexpat) and application dependencies (XStream, Spring Web), with 12 findings marked CRITICAL severity. The OpenSSL package (1.1.0j) dominates the list with 6 CVEs—three have available fixes (CVE-2022-1292, CVE-2022-0778, CVE-2021-3712/23840) and three do not (CVE-2022-2068, CVE-2022-2274), indicating the version is end-of-life and unsupported. Three additional CRITICAL findings lack fixes (CVE-2019-8457 in SQLite/libdb, CVE-2022-2068 in OpenSSL), while fixable CRITICALs exist for XStream (CVE-2013-7285), libexpat (CVE-2022-25236), and Spring Web (CVE-2016-1000027).

**Recommended Action:** Block this build. Immediately upgrade OpenSSL to a supported version (1.1.1 or 3.x series) to resolve 6 CVEs at once, upgrade XStream to ≥1.4.18, libexpat to ≥2.2.1, and Spring Web to ≥5.2.20. For unfixable CVEs (SQLite/libdb, OpenSSL 2068/2274), document compensating controls or plan component replacement. Do not proceed until OpenSSL is patched.
